claims.text: Let \(B\neq0\) be a commutative ring, \(A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}A_d\) a graded \(B\)-algebra with \(A_0=B\), \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge d_0}M_d\) a lower-bounded graded \(A\)-module. For homogeneous \(g_i\in M\), the \(g_i\) generate \(M\) over \(A\) iff their images generate \(Q:=M/A_+M\) over \(B\).

Under these hypotheses, every \(A\)-generating set of \(M\), homogeneous or not, maps to a \(B\)-generating set of \(Q\). Thus \(\mu_A(M)\ge\mu_B(Q)\), without any lower-boundedness or no-torsion assumption.

If \(B=\mathbb Z\) and \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) as a graded abelian group, then \(Q\) has a homogeneous \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(N\) elements; consequently \(\mu_A(M)=N\). Hence any already-known \(N\)-element homogeneous generating set of \(M\) is minimal.

Conditional application: if \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is a lower-bounded graded \(\Lambda\)-module with \(\Lambda_0=\mathbb Z\), and if \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), then every generating set of \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) has at least \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. Any displayed generating set having exactly \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements is therefore minimal.

Torsion caveat: \(\dim_{\mathbb Q}(Q\otimes\mathbb Q)=N\) proves only \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)\ge N\), not \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) nor an exact generator count. For \(Q=\mathbb Z^N\oplus\mathbb Z/2\), the rational dimension is \(N\), but \(Q\) requires more than \(N\) integral generators.

Lower-boundedness is essential for the converse. For \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(\deg x=1\), and \(M=\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]\), one has \(A_+M=xM=M\), hence \(M/A_+M=0\), although \(M\ne0\); this module is not bounded below.
